Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Redwood + Hypertune DevKit for LangChain/LlamaIndex telemetry

Hi Kimberly,

Great meeting last week — thanks for the time. Hypertune has a small engineering initiative to ship an "ISV DevKit" that makes it trivial for LangChain and LlamaIndex libraries to emit standardized tracing, prompt telemetry, and attribution hooks compatible with major inference runtimes.

We think Redwood's runtime tracing and token-level cost attribution would be a great downstream target to validate both reliability and cost/quality signals. Attached is a brief proposal with scope and a lightweight prototype plan (hypertune-devkit-proposal.pdf). Top-level goals:
- 1) One-line install for LangChain/LlamaIndex apps to send traces + prompts to Redwood.
- 2) Minimal perf overhead (instrumentation sampling + batching).
- 3) Example adapters and test harness for model/quantization variants.

Would Redwood be open to a small co-development pact: Hypertune engineers build the SDK bindings, Redwood provides runtime hooks, and both teams co-publish a joint devkit + docs? Our ask: engineering time for two 2-week sprints and security review.

Can you connect me to the right folks for an NDA and a draft SOW? Happy to hop on a 30-min sync — our availability this week: Tue/Thu 10–12 PT.

Thanks,

Alice Moreno
Director, Partnerships — Hypertune, Inc.
alice@hypertune.ai

Alice — thanks, this looks promising and aligns with a bunch of ISV traction we've been seeing.

Quick answers up front: we are interested in a co-dev approach. The things we care most about from Redwood's side are:
- Clear telemetry contract (events, sampling, token attribution) so our runtime can map traces to billing and quality diagnostics.
- Minimal changes required in user apps (prefers adapters over deep rewrites).
- Security/compliance gating: SOC2 evidence, data flow description, and optional allowlist of what leaves the customer environment.

I'll loop in Marissa (partnerships) and Vivek (runtime) so we can scope engineering and commercial asks. Could you attach a prototype or example repo (zip) and any preliminary license terms? Also curious whether Hypertune expects upstream changes to LangChain/LlamaIndex or if this will be an external adapter layer.

If Tue/Thu mornings work for you, let's hold Thu 10:30 PT — I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm.

Best,

Kimberly Park

- License: Apache 2.0 for the SDK; Hypertune is open to a permissive license or a CLA if Redwood prefers joint IP protections for co-branded assets.
- Security: our prototype supports customer-side sampling and redaction hooks; we can provide a dataflow diagram and SOC2 reference.

We'll prepare a draft SOW (technical scope + milestone-based deliverables) and an NDA template if Redwood wants. Thu 10:30 PT works — see calendar invite (I'll accept once you send).

Folks — looped Hypertune in; prototype attached. High-level thoughts before the Thu sync:

1) Commercial: propose a pilot deal (60 days) where Redwood provides runtime engineering support and joint go-to-market. For the pilot we can offer waived integration fees + a co-marketing credit if Hypertune commits to a public case study. Add an optional revenue share for referrals after GA.

2) Security: ask Hypertune for a short dataflow + SOC2 attest. We should scope the customer data types (prompt text, metadata) and define retention/allowlist controls.

3) Engineering: suggest two 2-week sprints from Hypertune to build the adapter + one 4-week sprint from Redwood to implement runtime hooks and QA. Vivek: can you sanity-check the timeline and resource ask?

4) IP/licensing: Marissa, recommend we propose Apache 2.0 on the SDK with a co-branding clause. If they want joint IP on the shared tooling (e.g., test harness) we can consider a simple joint ownership annex.

Next steps: Kimberly to confirm commercial terms and send a short SOW + DocuSign MSA link to Hypertune after Thu sync.

Thanks,

Kimberly
